summary: EASD 2026 in Milan (28 Sep–2 Oct) is driving most GLP-1 news this week. There are three kinds of opportunity. (1) New data landing right now: the retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 symposium is Wed 30 Sep, the Nordic registry found no pancreatic cancer signal with semaglutide, and Lilly and Novo released rival indirect comparisons (Zepbound vs Wegovy HD, Foundayo vs oral semaglutide, semaglutide 2 mg vs switching to tirzepatide). Mainstream news has picked these up, but health creators have made few explainers, so there's still an early window. (2) Questions people keep asking that got fresh hooks: hair loss (BMJ July plus NYU Sept), 'why isn't it working for me' (10–15% lose less than 5% in trials), protein now that McDonald's is building menus for GLP-1 users, and muscle protection (a new Clin Nutr piece on creatine). (3) Benefits beyond weight, framed carefully: fewer asthma attacks vs sulfonylureas (ERS, observational), stopping-treatment risk in veterans with T2D, and the SELECT mediation analysis, which is peaking. Every company-sponsored indirect comparison needs a 'not head-to-head' caveat and brand-neutral framing. We rejected the gray-market retatrutide story. Following the playbook, lead titles with the actual number plus the population and timeframe.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2: adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight/obesity lost up to 20.8% on average at 80 weeks (vs 4.0% placebo), full data at EASD Wed 30 Sep
candidates.angle: 'The first triple-hormone shot, explained': GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon in plain English, what 20.8% means (top dose, 80 weeks, people WITH type 2 diabetes, who usually lose less), A1C down up to 1.6 points from 7.7%, and the honest status: investigational, not approved as of Sept 2026. Mention GI side effects and discontinuation rates (3.8–11.6% vs 4.9% placebo).
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–5 days (symposium 30 Sep, then full paper/press cycle)
candidates.why_now: EASD symposium is Wed 30 Sep 08:30 CEST. It appeared in our last snapshot at 78 and has since gained mainstream pickup (Medical Daily EASD roundup, Lilly release). Retatrutide search interest is already high, and the gray-market buzz means people want a trustworthy explainer.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2: 1,152 adults with T2D + obesity/overweight; 12.7%/19.1%/20.8% loss at 4/9/12 mg vs 4.0% placebo at 80 weeks
Phase 3 retatrutide coverage, up to 22.6% weight loss in two trials
Retatrutide diabetes results headline EASD opening
TRIUMPH-2 registry entry NCT05929079

candidates.topic: Semaglutide not linked to pancreatic cancer: regulator-mandated Nordic registry study of 97,464 users with type 2 diabetes (EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: A reassuring myth-bust: 'Does Ozempic cause pancreatic cancer? 97,464 people in 3 countries say no signal.' Explain the hazard ratios (Denmark 1.00, Sweden 0.82, Norway 0.91, all with CIs crossing 1), the lack of any dose/duration trend, the comparison against other diabetes drugs, and the limits: observational, Novo-funded, adults with T2D.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EASD this week. Medscape, News-Medical and Medical Xpress picked it up 28–29 Sep. A separate global propensity-matched study (J Pers Med, 16 Sep) found no link to pancreatitis. This is a long-running fear, and creators haven't yet covered the new data.

evidence.signal: Registry data: no semaglutide–pancreatic cancer link, 97,464 users
Regulator-mandated study, Pottegård et al., Denmark/Sweden/Norway
Semaglutide not linked to higher pancreatic cancer risk
GLP-1 RAs not associated with pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer in T2D (global cohort)

candidates.topic: Zepbound vs Wegovy HD (7.2 mg): tirzepatide 10/15 mg linked to more weight loss at 72 weeks in a Lilly indirect comparison, not a head-to-head trial
candidates.angle: 'Which works better? Read the fine print first.' Recap the real head-to-head (SURMOUNT-5: 20.2% vs 13.7% at 72 weeks, adults with obesity without T2D). Then explain what an 'indirect treatment comparison' is and why a company-run ITC is weaker evidence. Close with: the best medicine is the one you and your prescriber pick for your health, coverage and tolerability.
keywords: which is better mounjaro or ozempic
candidates.why_now: Released 29 Sep and already covered by 10+ finance and news outlets. An Int J Obes indirect-comparison paper (28 Sep) covers the same question. 'Zepbound vs Wegovy' is a perennial high-volume search, and this gives it a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: Zepbound 10/15 mg associated with more weight loss than Wegovy HD in covariate-adjusted ITC
20.2% vs 13.7% at 72 weeks
Indirect efficacy/safety tirzepatide vs semaglutide, obesity without T2D

candidates.topic: Staying on track matters: interrupting GLP-1 treatment linked to up to 22% higher heart attack, stroke and death risk after 2 years off (333,000+ US veterans with type 2 diabetes, WashU)
candidates.angle: Frame it positively as 'why consistency matters for heart protection', not 'don't stop'. Stay observational ('linked to'), name the population (veterans with T2D), note that restarting restored protection only partly, and give the takeaway: if cost, side effects or supply are pushing you to stop, talk to your prescriber first. No switching or stopping advice.
keywords: what happens when you stop ozempic
candidates.why_now: Seen in 2 snapshots at a steady 84. The story is spreading through local TV (ABC15, NBC26), Fox and Reuters Health Rounds. Combined with this week's cost and subscription news (Newsom plan, cheaper providers), 'should I stop?' is a live audience question.

evidence.signal: Stopping GLP-1s can quickly erase cardiovascular benefits
Stopping Ozempic may raise heart attack and stroke risk
Press release, 333,000+ veterans, 3-year follow-up

candidates.topic: GLP-1 pills in 2026: Foundayo (orforglipron) 17.2 mg vs oral semaglutide 25 mg in type 2 diabetes, 1.5–2.4 points more weight loss and 0.3–0.6 points more A1C drop (indirect comparison, EASD)
candidates.angle: 'Pill vs pill, what we actually know': how the two oral GLP-1s differ (orforglipron is a small molecule with no fasting rule; oral semaglutide is a peptide taken on an empty stomach). Give the indirect result with its caveats (ACHIEVE-3 + PIONEER PLUS, not head-to-head). Add the ATTAIN post-hoc hook: similar weight loss across pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women.
candidates.why_now: Lilly release 29 Sep plus a menopause-stage post-hoc (News-Medical, Times of India, Medical Xpress). Foundayo is newly approved and being registered in more countries (Qatar), and 'GLP-1 pill' searches are climbing while explainer competition is still thin.

evidence.signal: Foundayo 17.2 mg vs oral semaglutide 25 mg ITC in T2D
Orforglipron vs oral semaglutide phase 3 (ACHIEVE-3) paper
Similar weight loss across three menopausal stages

candidates.topic: GLP-1 and hair loss: BMJ study found 53% higher relative risk of non-scarring hair loss vs SGLT2 users; NYU genetic study suggests extra risk in men already prone to pattern baldness
candidates.angle: A calm, practical explainer. Relative vs absolute risk. Shedding after rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium) is usually temporary. What helps: enough protein, iron and B12 checks with your clinician, and not losing weight too fast. Pattern-hair-loss-prone men can raise it with their doctor. No supplement cures.
keywords: does wegovy make your hair fall out
candidates.why_now: The Guardian (28 Sep) and Times of India (28 Sep) ran explainers on top of the NYU Sept study and the BMJ July paper. This is a top-10 GLP-1 side-effect search, and a solution-focused angle is underserved.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 drugs linked to increased hair loss risk (vs SGLT-2 and DPP-4 users)
NYU: GLP-1 may nudge genetically predisposed men toward hair loss
Does GLP-1 use result in significant hair loss?

candidates.topic: Semaglutide linked to up to ~40% fewer asthma attacks and ~20% fewer COPD flare-ups vs sulfonylureas (UK health records, ERS Congress 2026)
candidates.angle: A benefits-beyond-weight explainer with honest limits. Observational, compared with sulfonylurea users, people with T2D. Other GLP-1s (liraglutide, dulaglutide, exenatide) showed no such link. Researchers say don't start a GLP-1 for asthma outside guidance, and trials are needed. Possible mechanisms: less inflammation and less weight on the chest.
candidates.why_now: Medical Dialogues republished it 29 Sep, and it has earlier HCPLive, Pharmacy Times and ScienceDaily coverage. It hasn't reached mainstream consumer media or health creators yet. Autumn respiratory season makes it more relevant.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide can reduce asthma attacks by up to 40 per cent
Ozempic and Wegovy linked to nearly 40% fewer asthma attacks
20% fewer COPD flare-ups, other GLP-1s showed no association

candidates.topic: 'Why isn't my GLP-1 working?' About 14% in a semaglutide trial lost less than 5%. Slow responders, and what trials say about timing
candidates.angle: An encouraging, non-blaming explainer. Response varies (genetics, other conditions, other medicines). Some people are late responders (average ~25 weeks to reach 5% in one analysis). Weight isn't the only benefit: blood sugar, blood pressure and liver improve too. Bring these questions to your prescriber, with no dose or switching advice.
keywords: how long for ozempic to work
candidates.why_now: DongA Science (27 Sep) led on 'limited effect in up to 15%', and the Medscape 'When GLP-1s fall short' piece is circulating. It's a high-intent search question with emotional pull and few careful answers.

evidence.signal: Up to 15% of patients may be non-responders
As many as 1 in 5 won't lose much weight with GLP-1s
Some don't lose weight but still get liver and other benefits

candidates.topic: Fast food is redesigning menus for GLP-1 users (McDonald's: smaller portions, higher protein). What protein and portions actually matter on a GLP-1
candidates.angle: Use the culture hook to deliver the practical pillar: why protein matters when appetite drops (protecting muscle), simple protein-first plates, eating slowly, and fibre for constipation. Cite guidance and trial body-composition data, and don't endorse any brand. Title with a number, e.g. '30 million Americans on GLP-1s. Here's what the menus are chasing'.
candidates.why_now: CBS (28 Sep), Yahoo Finance and Fast Company (29 Sep) covered the McDonald's overhaul, and the shares moved 6%, so it's a mainstream curiosity hook that leads into our strongest evergreen pillar.

evidence.signal: How GLP-1 drugs are changing fast-food menus
McDonald's changing menu for the Ozempic era
Lean mass and musculoskeletal preservation in GLP-1-based obesity care

candidates.topic: Creatine to protect muscle on GLP-1s? New Clinical Nutrition commentary, but no GLP-1 trial results yet (RCTs now registered)
candidates.angle: 'Protein and lifting first, creatine maybe later': lean mass can make up a meaningful share of weight lost in trials. Resistance training and protein have the best evidence. Creatine is plausible but untested in GLP-1 users, and trials (e.g. NCT07625202) are underway. Anyone with kidney disease should check with a clinician. No dosing.
keywords: how to keep muscle on ozempic
candidates.why_now: Clin Nutr piece (21 Sep) plus newly registered creatine/GLP-1 trials. Supplement sellers are already pushing 'you must take creatine', so an honest correction is timely and fits our muscle-protection priority.

evidence.signal: Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss
Creatine supplementation during GLP-1a therapy RCT
12-week exercise + nutrition program to reduce muscle/bone loss on GLP-1

candidates.topic: CagriSema (cagrilintide + semaglutide) beat tirzepatide 5 mg: 12.4% vs 9.1% weight loss at 60 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes (REIMAGINE 5)
candidates.angle: Explain amylin, the 'other fullness hormone', and why pairing it with GLP-1 matters. Stay honest about the comparator: the lowest tirzepatide dose, in T2D, topline data from a company release. A1C drop was similar (non-inferior). Status: investigational as of Sept 2026.
candidates.why_now: Topline 21 Sep, then Pharmacy Times (28 Sep) and a NewsNation 'outperforms Zepbound' headline that overstates it. A Diabetes Ther review of amylin agonists also landed 28 Sep. The fix-the-headline angle gives us something different to say.

evidence.signal: CagriSema bests tirzepatide for weight loss in adults with T2D
REIMAGINE 5 topline 12.4% vs 9.1%
New amylin-based agonists review

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and rare 'eye stroke' (NAION): what the studies show, how rare it is, and which symptoms mean call a doctor
candidates.angle: Calm, factual safety literacy, not fear. Specialist societies say the overall risk is low and causation isn't proven. Name the warning sign (sudden painless vision loss in one eye means urgent care). Tell viewers to mention eye history to their prescriber. No lawsuit framing, and no stopping advice.
candidates.why_now: Boston.com blindness lawsuit (28 Sep), a Boston Globe explainer (22 Sep), and the Medical Economics 'highest risk with Wegovy' mention. Fear-driven searches are rising, and a reassuring, accurate explainer can serve them.

evidence.signal: Wegovy may have highest eye-stroke signal among semaglutide products (pharmacovigilance)
What GLP-1 users should know about rare vision loss; societies say risk is low
Could GLP-1s be linked to rare vision loss?

candidates.angle: The topic is peaking, so we need a different angle: 'Your heart benefit isn't just the scale.' Pair it with the Diabetes Care predictors paper (who lost the most in SELECT) and MUSC's 'ABCs of heart prevention now include GLP'. Use the exact SELECT population.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 8 snapshots with slowly declining momentum (76 to 70). News-Medical and Medical Daily re-covered it 28–29 Sep. Still worth one differentiated carousel.

candidates.topic: Nausea, constipation and 'is it gastroparesis?' Making common GLP-1 GI side effects easier (new 2026 expert review + Cedars-Sinai explainer)
candidates.angle: Useful and reassuring. GI effects are the most common side effects and are usually worst early on and when doses go up. Evidence-based habits help: smaller meals, stop at comfortably full, go easy on greasy food, fluids, fibre. Know the red flags (persistent vomiting, severe belly pain) that mean call your clinician. Also tell anyone due for endoscopy or surgery to tell the care team they're on a GLP-1.
keywords: how to reduce nausea on wegovy
candidates.why_now: Nutr Clin Pract expert review (Oct 2026 issue) plus a Cedars-Sinai explainer on 29 Sep. Side-effect searches are steady and high, and this is one of the playbook's double-down pillars.

candidates.topic: Eat slower, feel fuller? Eating rate and satiety with ultra-processed foods (Eur J Nutr secondary analysis of a randomized crossover trial)
candidates.angle: The natural side of GLP-1: why eating pace matters for fullness signals (the gut hormones, GLP-1 among them). The study measured satiety responsiveness, not GLP-1 levels, so say that. Practical tips: texture, pace, protein-first. Never framed as a replacement for the medicine.
candidates.why_now: New RCT secondary analysis (24 Sep). 'Natural GLP-1' is a high-volume search full of misinformation ('nature's Ozempic'), so a correct, gentle alternative has an opening.

evidence.signal: Satiety responsiveness after UPF differing in texture-derived eating rate, randomized crossover

candidates.angle: Who qualifies (adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and obesity), what SURMOUNT-OSA measured (breathing events per hour), and that it works alongside CPAP rather than replacing it on your own. Bring these questions to a sleep doctor.
candidates.why_now: Yahoo Health 'Should you take a GLP-1 to treat OSA?' (28 Sep) and Vera Health coverage. Autumn clock changes (AU 4 Oct, UK 25 Oct, US 1 Nov) bring sleep interest back.
